albums.description: A knotty, chameleonic indie rock record mixing jangle, synths and drum machines. At least one song sounds like a lost Pavement track, making it a rewarding listen for fans of homemade, shape-shifting guitar pop.
albums.lineage: Continues Zook's homemade jangle/synth-pop hybrid songwriting, which sounds indebted to Pavement's slacker guitar-pop.

albums.label: Lame-O Records
albums.description: A sprawling double set of concise, hook-driven power pop split into 'Girls' and 'Boys' halves, led by Peter Gill, who also plays in Friendship. The songs are quick, bright and jangly, flying past before they can outstay their welcome. It suits listeners who like power pop in big, generous doses.
albums.lineage: Gill's membership in Friendship ties 2nd Grade to the same Philadelphia scene as Friendship and Hurry; the songwriting sounds indebted to Big Star and Guided by Voices.

albums.label: Ever/Never Records
albums.description: This New York quartet's self-titled debut is a hooky, jangly and twangy power-pop rock record with blistering riffs and meaty choruses, released by the fast-rising Ever/Never label. It's punchy and immediate, favoring rock and roll swagger over polish. It's for fans who want the twang-adjacent side of the current power-pop wave.
albums.lineage: Signed to the New York label Ever/Never, which ties the band into the current DIY jangle/twang underground.

albums.album: Well Once There Was A King
albums.label: Historic NJ Recordings
albums.description: A sprawling grab-bag from a home-recording project, Well Once There Was A King cycles through folk, slacker jangle, country, doom-metal detours and Beach Boys harmonies without pausing for breath. It rewards the same magpie curiosity that draws people to Guided by Voices' overstuffed records.
albums.lineage: Sounds indebted to the lo-fi, kitchen-sink home-taping tradition of GBV and Sebadoh, filtered through a 2020s Bandcamp DIY sensibility.
key_tracks: Well Once There Was A King

albums.label: Angel Tapes
albums.description: This trio's debut full-length channels raucous energy into hook-forward, dynamic indie rock, packing frantic drive and earworm melodies into a lean runtime. Delicate falsetto verses give way to explosive, unrelenting choruses across the tracklist. It's for fans who want their power pop with real teeth.
albums.lineage: Released via Fire Talk's Angel Tapes imprint, which ties the band into the current DIY guitar-pop underground.

albums.label: Run For Cover Records
albums.description: Hunt's most maximalist record yet trades home recording for a fuller studio sound, with frantic late-'90s pop-rock hooks, autotuned detours and euphoric grooves recalling Screamadelica. It still sounds instantly familiar despite its left turns, the fullest treatment his songwriting has gotten to date.
albums.lineage: Hunt's self-released catalog moving from bedroom recording toward a bigger studio sound while keeping the same playful, hook-heavy songwriting.
key_tracks: Waiting for You to Come Home

albums.label: Keeled Scales
albums.description: This Brooklyn band's debut, originally formed in North Carolina, eschews the twang-and-shoegaze sound of their home-state peers for something more its own: brutal, pounding riffs paired with dual lead vocals and patiently pastoral arrangement shifts. Released by the Texas label Keeled Scales, it stands apart from the countrygaze pack while sharing its scene. It's for fans who want the loudest, least twangy corner of the current DIY guitar-rock underground.
albums.lineage: Formed within North Carolina's twang-and-shoegaze scene before relocating to Brooklyn; its sound sits between C4 countrygaze and straighter, heavier guitar rock.

albums.label: Ruination Record Co.
albums.description: A Brooklyn songwriter's guitar-and-synth indie rock record, made with players from the Ruination Record Co. circle. Clean guitars and glowing synths frame understated vocals and mid-tempo songs. It suits listeners who like thoughtful, low-key indie rock.
albums.lineage: Part of the same small Brooklyn songwriter-collaborator scene as Adeline Hotel, Office Culture and The Bird Calls.

albums.label: Self-released
albums.description: A batch of scrappy rock sketches built on Telecaster-driven hooks and guitar charm. The earworm rippers mix Nuggets garage and '90s indie jangle with punk swagger, most of them over in about two minutes.
albums.lineage: Sounds indebted to Nuggets-era garage rock and '90s indie jangle.

albums.label: Self-released
albums.description: Cooper's third album trades the jam-guitar sound of her earlier band for a crisper, Beck-like mix of fuzz bass, piano and twinkling synths. It is warm, direct pop-rock songwriting with a slacker's DIY informality, for listeners who like hooks with a homemade edge.
albums.lineage: Sounds like a former jam/psych-rock guitarist moving toward a more concise, jangle-adjacent indie-pop songwriting style.

albums.label: Get Better Records
albums.description: An anthemic yet intimate pop-rock record that sits between energetic and vulnerable songwriting. It continues the band's move from scrappy Philadelphia basement pop-punk toward bigger power-pop hooks.
albums.lineage: Latest chapter of Remember Sports' Philadelphia DIY power-pop lineage.

albums.label: ANTI-
albums.description: Slow Pulp's third album continues the band's move toward pristine, contemporary alt-rock that melds 1990s shoegaze scale with direct pop songwriting. The emotional stakes run higher and the production is more polished, for fans who liked Yard's balance of noise and melody.
albums.lineage: A continuation of Yard's shoegaze-meets-Americana synthesis, pushing further into polished, radio-ready alt-rock.

albums.label: Matador
albums.description: Lindsey Jordan's third Snail Mail album follows Valentine with clear-eyed, jangling guitar-pop, keeping the conversational, unadorned vocal delivery that made Lush a breakout. Harmonized guitars and a breezy, hushed touch carry songs about heartbreak, for listeners who want confessional indie rock without much studio gloss.
albums.lineage: Continues Snail Mail's own lineage from Lush through Valentine, staying within confessional, guitar-led jangle-pop songwriting.

albums.label: Curation Records
albums.description: A Los Angeles band's debut LP, blending frantic C86-style jangle-pop with post-punk urgency and a touch of Flying Nun. Ten songs of tightly wound guitar interplay and restless energy.
albums.lineage: A direct 2020s continuation of the Flying Nun/C86 jangle lineage that runs through this whole lane.

albums.label: Merge Records
albums.description: The London 'Celtic jangle boyband' moves to Merge for its third album, pushing its shimmering, virtuosic guitar-pop further with folk touches and a second, steelier vocal presence arguing against Owen Williams's familiar persona across songs about grief and regret. It's the most ambitious Tubs record yet.
albums.lineage: Builds directly on Dead Meat and Cotton Crown's jangle-pop songwriting, deepening the band's British folk-jangle hybrid.

albums.label: Self-released
albums.description: The Indianapolis band's follow-up to Triple Seven continues their blend of fuzzy shoegaze guitar textures with unabashedly sweet, jangling pop melodies. It keeps the same sugar-and-noise balance that made Triple Seven a breakout.
albums.lineage: Continues Wishy's fusion of shoegaze guitar-wall production with 1990s power-pop songwriting established on Triple Seven.

albums.label: Self-released
albums.description: kitship's am i a rock? is low-key acoustic singer-songwriter fare and understated lo-fi indie rock, built on commanding vocals and instant, unfussy melodies. It suits listeners who like scrappy, tuneful home recordings.
albums.lineage: Sounds akin to the current Chicago Bandcamp slacker/lo-fi network around acts like Sharp Pins.
